chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) told us: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Siyari, from Ibn Baqqah, from Abd al-Salam, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying:
It is to deny the blessings that a man says: 'I ate such and such food, and it harmed me.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.كَفَرَ بِالنِّعَمِ: Denying the blessings (specifically in the context of gratitude and attribution)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to 'deny the blessings' in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that 'denying blessings' (kufr bi al-ni'am) is often a subtle ethical lapse rather than theological apostasy. It specifically warns against complaining about permissible sustenance, as such grumbling reflects a failure to recognize God's will and constitutes ingratitude (qillat al-shukr). This highlights the Shia emphasis on cultivating a positive, grateful disposition even in minor daily actions like eating.
